introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. History 3 (0760), Paper 3 - Africa and World History, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Candidates are required to answer FOUR questions, choosing ONE from each of the four sections (Section A: Africa, 1800-1945; Section B: Africa, 1945 to the present; Section C: World Revolutions and Diplomacy, 1700-1919; Section D: World, 1919 to the present date). All questions carry equal marks (25 marks each).

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Points : chaque question porte 25 marks imprimés (« All questions carry equal marks »), soit 100 points pour les quatre questions à traiter. Aucun écart de points constaté ; `points` vaut 25 pour l'exercice et pour l'unique question de chaque fichier.

Sujet scanné de deux pages (page de garde, puis les questions 1 à 12 réparties en quatre sections de trois questions) : filigranes gcerevision.com ignorés ; aucune question coupée ni illisible, aucune figure ni carte dans le sujet.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au niveau Advanced Level (introduction, développement, conclusion argumentée). Aucune citation ni statistique précise n'est avancée ; les dates, noms, traités et lieux sont ceux de l'historiographie établie, cités de mémoire historique et à faire relire par un historien avant mise en vente.

Question 11 : faits cités de mémoire historique (conférences de Yalta février 1945 et de Potsdam été 1945, discours de Fulton en mars 1946, doctrine Truman mars 1947, plan Marshall 1947-48, Kominform 1947, blocus de Berlin juin 1948 - mai 1949, OTAN avril 1949, première bombe soviétique 1949, victoire communiste en Chine octobre 1949, guerre de Corée 1950-53, Pacte de Varsovie 1955, Spoutnik 1957, mur de Berlin 1961, crise de Cuba octobre 1962, accords d'Helsinki 1975, chute du mur de Berlin novembre 1989, dissolution de l'URSS décembre 1991) ; aucun chiffre militaire ou budgétaire n'est donné.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Analyse the causes and consequences of the Cold War after 1945.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The Cold War was the long struggle between the United States and the Soviet Union, and their allies, from the end of the Second World War until about 1991. It was called "cold" because the two superpowers never fought each other directly: the rivalry was carried on through ideology, propaganda, alliances, the arms race and wars in other countries. The causes lay in the differences and mistrust between the wartime allies, and the consequences were felt all over the world, including Africa.

**1. Causes.**
- *Ideological conflict.* The United States led the capitalist and democratic West, while the Soviet Union led communism. Each saw the other as a threat to its way of life, and the mistrust dated from the Russian Revolution of 1917.
- *Wartime tension.* Although they allied against Hitler, the Soviet Union had signed a pact with Germany in 1939 and Stalin resented the delay in opening a second front in Western Europe. At the Yalta conference (February 1945) and the Potsdam conference (July-August 1945) there were disagreements about the future of Poland and Germany, and about reparations. The death of Roosevelt and the new, firmer attitude of Truman, and the American possession of the atomic bomb, raised Soviet suspicions.
- *Soviet control in Eastern Europe.* The Red Army occupied Eastern Europe, and Stalin installed pro-Soviet governments in Poland, Romania, Bulgaria, Hungary and later Czechoslovakia (1948), to create a buffer against the West. Winston Churchill described this at Fulton in 1946 as an "iron curtain" across Europe.
- *American policy of containment.* The Truman Doctrine (March 1947) promised aid to countries threatened by communism, beginning with Greece and Turkey. The Marshall Plan (1947-48) gave economic aid to rebuild Western Europe, which the Soviet Union rejected, replying with the Cominform (1947) and Comecon (1949).
- *The division of Germany and the Berlin crisis.* In 1948 the Western zones introduced a new currency, and the Soviets blockaded West Berlin (June 1948 to May 1949); the Western Allies supplied the city by the Berlin Airlift. Germany was then divided into the Federal Republic (West) and the German Democratic Republic (East) in 1949.
- *Military alliances and events in Asia.* NATO was formed in April 1949, and the Warsaw Pact in 1955. The Soviet Union tested an atomic bomb in 1949, and the communist victory in China in 1949 and the Korean War (1950-53) made the rivalry global.

**2. Consequences.**
- *Division of Europe and the world.* An "Iron Curtain" divided Europe into East and West, and Germany and Berlin were divided, symbolised by the Berlin Wall built in 1961. Many other countries were pressed to choose a camp.
- *The arms race and the nuclear threat.* Both sides built large stocks of nuclear weapons, and the world lived under fear of nuclear war. The Cuban Missile Crisis (October 1962) brought the two close to nuclear war. The space race (for example the Soviet satellite Sputnik in 1957) became a part of the competition.
- *Proxy wars.* The superpowers supported opposing sides in local wars: Korea, Vietnam, the Middle East, and in Africa, such as the Congo in the early 1960s, Angola, and the Horn of Africa. These wars cost many lives and destroyed economies.
- *Effects on international organisations.* The rivalry paralysed the United Nations Security Council through the veto, and the Non-Aligned Movement (arising from the Bandung Conference of 1955 and the Belgrade Conference of 1961) was formed by states which refused to join either camp.
- *Effects on decolonisation and Africa.* The superpowers' opposition to colonial empires encouraged independence, but after independence African states were drawn into the rivalry through aid, military support and ideological alliances, and some leaders were overthrown or supported according to their alignment. Cameroon, like many francophone states, kept ties with the West.
- *Economic effects.* The USA and USSR spent heavily on weapons, and the West recovered with Marshall aid, while Eastern European economies were controlled by Moscow.
- *Détente and the end of the Cold War.* Tension eased in the 1970s with arms control agreements (SALT) and the Helsinki Accords of 1975, returned in the early 1980s, and ended with the reforms of Mikhail Gorbachev (glasnost and perestroika), the fall of the Berlin Wall in November 1989, the reunification of Germany in 1990, and the collapse of the Soviet Union in December 1991. The United States emerged as the sole superpower.

**Conclusion.** The Cold War arose from ideological opposition, wartime mistrust, Soviet expansion in Eastern Europe and the American policy of containment, and it shaped world politics for almost half a century through the division of Europe, the arms race, proxy wars and the alignment of the new states, until the collapse of communism in Europe and the Soviet Union ended it.
